description.narrative: The cooperation aims to build trust between people divided by the contact line through dialogue and discreet joint efforts to address shared challenges, complementing the Track 1 peace process. This is supported by policy ideas from the Black Sea dialogue group to enhance predictability in the maritime zone, joint preventive and environmental projects under the JEDI format to avert disasters near the frontline, and humanitarian solutions proposed by civil society, which are fed into peace talks or exchanged between conflict parties.

title.narrative: Innovative ideas for dealing with the tensions in the Black Sea are conveyed to decision-making circles.
Briefing of decision makers and affiliated experts.

target.value: Participants have worked to define a common understanding of the threats in the Black Sea region, and their dialogue process has drawn on lessons learned from other shared waterways (eg Scandinavia, South China Sea).

actual.value: In the Black Sea track, HD continued to help the UN to implement the Russia-Ukraine grain deal at the JCC in Istanbul.

target.value: Concepts and ideas developed in the Black Sea have been presented to experts and or officials of concerned state institutions.

title.narrative: Joint preventive measures and end environmental projects are devised by experts in the Joint Ecological Dialogue Initiative, or JEDI format that contribute to averting a disaster near the frontline.
The Joint Ecological Dialogue initiative (JEDI) meets regular and develops proposals on how to address ecological problems in the region.

target.value: Participants have agreed and implemented informal mechanisms for dealing with emerging ecological problems.

actual.value: Joint preventive measures and environmental projects are devised by experts in the Joint Ecological Dialogue Initiative, or JEDI format that contribute to averting a disaster near the frontline

target.value: 3-4 options developed. The JEDI group has established cooperative mechanisms to mitigate ecological risks and prevent an ecological disaster. These are taken up by decision-makers and in official negotiations.

title.narrative: Policy options ideas developed by the Black Sea dialogue group that contribute to making behavior in the maritime zone more predictable, with a view of avoiding a miscalculation or re-escalation.

A group of political and maritime experts engages regularly in a substantial discussion about joint problems and opportunities for trilateral collaboration in the Black Sea, and develops concrete proposals for improved cooperation.

target.value: The experts have identified mutually agreed options for managing tensions in the Black Sea and promote these ideas among decision-makers in their respective capitals.
Participants in the expert dialogue have defined common interests and threats, solidified a regular dialogue process and developed scenarios and/or roadmaps for finding common solutions.

actual.value: Participants in our ecological group worked together to come up with potential solutions to the problems of disused mines, critical infrastructure protection and nuclear safety.
